二十世紀中葉，取樣器的前身是播放磁帶錄音的鍵盤樂器；Mellotron 在196: In the mid-twentieth century the sampler's forerunners were keyboards that played tape recordings; the Mellotron was used by many bands in the late 1960s and the 1970s but was expensive and bulky, with a range of at most three octaves. Around 1969 the EMS Musys system carried out early digital sampling; in 1976 the Computer Music Melodian became the first sampling synthesizer sold commercially, and in 1979 the Australian Fairlight CMI became the first polyphonic digital sampling synthesizer. Prices fell in the 1980s and the E-mu Emulator and Ensoniq Mirage brought samplers into wide use; in 1987 the E-mu SP-1200 and in 1988 the Akai MPC60 pushed their use in hip hop, while the Ensoniq EPS turned towards live performance. In the 2010s music workstations commonly integrated sampling.

取樣器主要由電子與機械組件構成。其核心為數位處理器與微晶片，負責聲音的採集、儲存: The sampler is built mainly from electronic and mechanical components. At its core are a digital processor and microchips, which capture, store and play back sound. The case is usually plastic or aluminium alloy, for durable protection. The keyboard uses rubber or plastic keys over metal springs. Storage is on a hard disk or solid-state chips. The audio outputs use gold-plated or copper connectors to keep the signal clean. Some high-end models have wooden panels and leather handles, both handsome and practical.

A beginner first loads or records a sample, assigns the sound to a key range and sets the root note and pitch tracking; pressing a key then plays the sample, and velocity can change the layer. More advanced work adjusts filtering, effects, looping and multi-timbral set-ups. The source gives no teaching repertoire or playing position.

Early digital sampling was used in Harrison Birtwistle's Chronometer; in the early 1980s Japanese electronic music groups used samplers to sample and loop, and synth-pop musicians used them too. In hip hop, digital samplers are commonly used to make beats.

The sampler is an electrophone: it records, samples and edits all kinds of sound, storing rhythms, melodies, speech, effects or longer musical passages in digital memory and playing them back from an attached MIDI keyboard, sequencer or other trigger device. A single sample can be transposed into scales and chords, and samplers usually offer filtering, effects, low-frequency modulation, multiple timbres and polyphony. Players use them in modern music production, to imitate other instruments, or for live sound effects on the theatre stage. The source gives no H-S number and no specific family composition.
取樣器的音色具有高度多樣性，因其能夠錄製和重現任何聲源。其音質可從明亮清晰到深沉: The sampler's timbre is extremely varied, because it can record and reproduce any sound source. Its tone may be bright and clear or deep and heavy, depending on the sound sampled. In theory its range covers the whole audible frequency spectrum, from the very lowest sub-bass to the sharpest highs. Its resonance is distinctive: digital synthesis and electronic amplification can keep or change the resonating character of the original. Compared with traditional instruments, the sampler offers an unlimited range of timbres — it can imitate the warmth of a piano and the softness of strings, and it can also make the cold texture of an electronic instrument. Its hallmark is the plasticity of the sound, which allows real-time processing and transposition, giving a rich passage between natural and artificial, organic and electronic.
